characters.name: King Arthur
characters.description: The central king, sovereign of Britain and leader of the Round Table; conducts wars, holds courts and quests, later wounded in final battle.

characters.name: Merlin
characters.description: A powerful wizard and prophet who advises kings (foretells Arthur's coming, arranges events, later trapped by Vivien).

characters.name: Vortigern
characters.description: The usurper king in London whose tower fails until Merlin reveals the cause.

characters.name: Ambrosius
characters.description: One of the opponents of Vortigern mentioned among the northern challenge to the usurper (appears as a name in Merlin's prophecy); associated with Aurelius Ambrosius.

characters.name: Aurelius Ambrosius
characters.description: Called Aurelius or Aurelius Ambrosius; a rightful king who defeats Vortigern and whose actions bring Merlin into play (linked to Stonehenge episode).

characters.name: Uther Pendragon
characters.description: Father of Arthur; king who takes Igerna as wife, aided by Merlin, and fathered Arthur by Merlin's device; called Uther Pendragon after making dragon banners.

characters.name: Gillomanius
characters.description: King in Ireland who resists the taking of the Giants' Dance (Stonehenge stones).

characters.name: Gorlois
characters.description: Duke of Cornwall whose wife Igerna is desired by Uther; slain in battle.

characters.name: Igerna
characters.description: Wife of Gorlois, later married to Uther; mother of Arthur (unnamed as mother in narrative but referred to as Igerna).

characters.name: Merlin's master Blaise
characters.description: Hermit named Blaise who nourished Merlin in youth and records Merlin's accounts at his direction.

characters.name: Lady of the Lake
characters.description: Mysterious lady who presents Excalibur (and its scabbard) by means of an arm out of the lake; multiple lake-ladies act in story.

characters.name: Sir Ector
characters.description: Arthur's foster-father who raises Arthur as his son and appears at Arthur's drawing of the sword; father of Sir Key.

characters.name: Sir Key
characters.description: Foster-brother of Arthur (Sir Ector's son), later High Steward of England in Arthur's reign; also called Sir Key the seneschal.

characters.name: Brice, Archbishop of Canterbury
characters.description: Archbishop who convenes the nobles before the stone and sword and presides at Arthur's coronation ceremonies.

characters.name: Sir Ulfius
characters.description: A loyal knight and adviser to Arthur, participating in early battles and offices (chamberlain role earlier).

characters.name: Sir Brastias
characters.description: A knight and companion of Arthur in early battles (named participant in fights).

characters.name: Sir Griflet
characters.description: Young squire-turned-knight who serves Arthur and is involved in early combats and rescues (also wounded and healed).

characters.name: Sir Lucas the butler
characters.description: A knight identified as 'Sir Lucas the butler' who appears as participant in battles.

characters.name: The white dragon
characters.description: A symbolic dragon seen beneath the pool in Merlin's prophecy, representing the Saxon invaders in the vision.

characters.name: The red dragon
characters.description: The opposing dragon in Merlin's vision, representing the British (or vice versa in prophecy); seen fighting the white dragon.

characters.name: Sir Balin le Savage
characters.description: A knight who obtains a magical sword and, through the Dolorous Stroke, causes grievous harm (kills and later mortally wounds his brother Sir Balan).

characters.name: Sir Balan
characters.description: Brother of Sir Balin who fights and tragically mortally wounds his brother in mistaken encounter; later dies beside him.

characters.name: King Lot
characters.description: A king of Orkney and a frequent antagonist of Arthur; father of Gawain and his brothers.

characters.name: Belisent
characters.description: Half-sister of Arthur who visits and later is mother of Gawain and his brothers (called King's half-sister Belisent).

characters.name: Sir Gawain
characters.description: Arthur's nephew and one of his chief knights; central in many adventures and later in conflict with Lancelot; leading judge and avenger.

characters.name: Gawain's brothers (Gaheris, Agravaine, Gareth)
characters.description: Sons of King Lot and Belisent; Gaheris and Agravaine figure in plots and deeds (Gareth also known as Beaumains).

characters.name: Sir Mador de la Port
characters.description: Knight whose kinsman Sir Patrice is killed by a poisoned apple; he accuses Guinevere and demands trial by combat.

characters.name: Sir Patrice (Patrice)
characters.description: The knight who dies from a poisoned apple at Guinevere's banquet; his death sparks the accusation against the queen.

characters.name: Sir Pinell le Savage
characters.description: The knight who actually poisons the apple that kills Sir Patrice (later identified by the Lady of the Lake).

characters.name: Queen Guinevere
characters.description: Arthur's queen whose alleged betrayal and later rescue by Lancelot precipitate the realm's schism and final wars.

characters.name: Sir Lancelot
characters.description: Preeminent knight of the Round Table; Arthur's greatest warrior and Guinevere's favorite; central to many adventures and to the kingdom's downfall.

characters.name: Sir Bors
characters.description: A kinsman and faithful companion of Lancelot; acts as Lancelot's intermediary and later participates in quests and combats.

characters.name: Sir Lionel
characters.description: A kinsman of Lancelot (also son of Ban) and participant in many adventures; fights alongside Lancelot.

characters.name: Sir Pellinore
characters.description: A chivalric but sometimes quarrelsome knight who follows the Questing Beast; father of Sir Tor and others.

characters.name: The Questing Beast
characters.description: A strange mythical creature pursued by Pellinore and others; described with a leopard's body, serpent head and lion's tail.

characters.name: Sir Tor
characters.description: A youth raised as a cowherd's son but revealed as King Pellinore's son; proves himself and is later admitted to the Round Table.

characters.name: Sir Griflet (young Griflet)
characters.description: A youth who petitions for knighthood, is knighted by Arthur and performs early service and adventures.

characters.name: Sir Tristram (Tristram)
characters.description: Tristram of Lyonesse (also Tristan/Tristram), famed lover and knight; central in the tragic tale of La Belle Isault (Isolde).

characters.name: La Belle Isault
characters.description: Also called Isault or Isolde; the Irish princess healed and loved by Tristram; central to Tristram's personal storyline.

characters.name: King Mark
characters.description: King of Cornwall; uncle of Tristram and later husband of La Belle Isault; often jealous and at odds with Tristram.

characters.name: King Ban of Benwick
characters.description: Father of Lancelot (King Ban) mentioned as ancestor; his realm provides part of Lancelot's origin.

characters.name: King Bors of Gaul
characters.description: Ally of Arthur who aids in battles; father or kin to Lancelot's supporters (named King Bors of Gaul).

characters.name: Sir Palomedes
characters.description: A valiant, unchristened knight who fights in many tournaments and tournaments against Arthur's men and Tristram.

characters.name: Sir Bleoberis de Ganis
characters.description: A knight cousin to Lancelot who participates in tournaments and deeds; aids Tristram and others.

characters.name: Sir Dinadan
characters.description: A Knight of the Round Table known for wit and occasional reluctance to rash deeds; companion of Tristram in adventures.

characters.name: Sir Lamoracke
characters.description: A renowned knight introduced in the narrative; noted for prowess and later associated with the Grail tales and other adventures.

characters.name: King Pelles
characters.description: The maimed or wounded king (kinsman of Joseph of Arimathea) whose pain results from Balin's Dolorous Stroke and who is healed only by the Grail knights.

characters.name: Joseph of Arimathea
characters.description: Biblical figure credited with bringing the Holy Grail to Britain and whose lineage and treasures feature in the Grail lore.

characters.name: King Evelake
characters.description: An ancient king associated with Joseph of Arimathea's missions; later appears maimed and healed in Grail narrative.

characters.name: Sir Galahad
characters.description: The pure knight created/introduced at the court; sits in the Siege Perilous and succeeds in the Quest for the Holy Grail, achieving its fulfillment and dying in grace.

characters.name: Sir Percival
characters.description: A Grail knight whose adventures include healing and quests; meets Galahad and Bors in Grail narrative and later becomes a hermit.

characters.name: Sir Bors the Younger (the Grail knight)
characters.description: One of the three knights (with Galahad and Percival) who successfully see the Grail; later returns and survives to tell of events.

characters.name: Nacien the hermit
characters.description: A holy hermit who counsels ladies and knights and gives instruction about the Grail quest (issues counsel to avoid ladies on Grail quest).

characters.name: The maiden (Percival's sister)
characters.description: Sister of Sir Percival who helps and dies for others in Grail episodes; identified as 'Sir Percival's sister' in the text.

characters.name: Sir Bedivere
characters.description: Arthur's loyal knight who survives to return Excalibur to the water and bears witness to Arthur's last acts.

characters.name: Sir Lucan
characters.description: One of Arthur's household knights who helps bear Arthur after the final battle and dies of his wounds at Arthur's side.

characters.name: Sir Modred
characters.description: Arthur's nephew/illegitimate son who seizes authority in Arthur's absence, incites rebellion, and fatally wounds Arthur in final conflict.

characters.name: Sir Bernard of Astolat
characters.description: Baron of Astolat who shelters Lancelot; father of the Maid of Astolat (Elaine).

characters.name: Elaine of Astolat (The Maid of Astolat)
characters.description: Also called the Fair Maid of Astolat; falls hopelessly in love with Lancelot, nurses him, and dies of a broken heart; sent to court in a funerary barge.

characters.name: Sir Lavaine
characters.description: A young knight of Astolat who serves Lancelot in tournaments and aids him; son of Sir Bernard.

characters.name: Sir Melerance / Meliance of Lis
characters.description: A knight mentioned among tourneying knights whom the Maid with Narrow Sleeves admires; appears in that episode.

characters.name: The Maid with the Narrow Sleeves
characters.description: A young unnamed damsel who challenges Sir Gawain and the company with her 'narrow sleeves' token—central to the chapter 'Sir Gawain and the Maid with the Narrow Sleeves.'

aliases.text: the Maid with the Narrow Sleeves

characters.name: Sir Percival's hermit aunt (the recluse)
characters.description: A pious recluse and aunt to Percival who informs him of his kin and guides him toward Grail-related quests.

characters.name: Sir Gahalatine
characters.description: A knight of the lists that opposes Bagdemagus; mentioned in Bagdemagus' tournament adventures.

characters.name: King Anguish of Ireland
characters.description: King of Ireland who sends Marhaus to demand tribute and later interacts with Tristram and Isault; called King Anguish.

characters.name: Sir Marhaus
characters.description: Irish champion sent to secure tribute who fights Tristram and is mortally wounded (piece of blade found in his head).

characters.name: Sir Palomedes (duplicate entry check)
characters.description: Included earlier; valiant tournament knight who later fights Tristram and others.

characters.name: Sir Perin de Mountbelgard
characters.description: A knight allied in the quests who is slain by magic abuse in one episode (companion of others).

characters.name: Sir Herleus
characters.description: A knight mentioned as slain in ambush (companion to Balin); pleads his steward to pursue revenge.

characters.name: Sir Garlon
characters.description: A treacherous invisible knight who kills by witchcraft; slain by Balin; name appears in Perceval-derived episode.

characters.name: Sir Bagdemagus
characters.description: A king and knight who is aided by Lancelot in a tournament and who later features in adventures connected to Lancelot's imprisonment by queens.

characters.name: Sir Tor (duplicate entry check)
characters.description: Included earlier; son of Pellinore and Cornish-raised youth made knight by Arthur.

characters.name: King Claudas
characters.description: Mentioned as adversary in Gaul who works mischief against Ban and Bors; appears as background antagonist.

characters.name: Sir Accolon of Gaul
characters.description: Knight tricked by Morgan le Fay into fighting Arthur with Excalibur (secretly given to Accolon); later dies, confessing the treason.

characters.name: Queen Morgan le Fay
characters.description: Arthur's half-sister, a sorceress who enchants and plots (steals Excalibur, schemes against Arthur, traps Merlin).

characters.name: Sir Modred (duplicate check)
characters.description: Included earlier; appears as the traitor who claims kingship and whose rebellion brings about Arthur's final battle.
